scope: One identical 5-second timeline shot, 81 native frames at 720x1280/16fps; no claim about long-film identity consistency.

nativeProfiler.note: Log-derived subphase timings, not retroactively inserted into the original runtime receipt. First step slower; cause not conclusively measured.

visualReview.method: 10 chronological full-scene frames plus four original-resolution face crops, and full FFmpeg decoding of the clip. Human review remains required.
findings: More visible upward head and gaze movement in accelerated shot; original is subtler and becomes softer later.
No obvious person swap or extra limbs in the inspected frames; identity not certified and not tested across scenes.
Room, shirt and wall-clock composition retained.
No generated subtitle overlay observed in inspected frames; original clock markings are present.
Requested gaze is still toward the bright window rather than clearly toward the wall clock; daylight in the shared input does not become the requested night.
Different native encoders/bitrate: accelerated native file is much smaller. Codec/settings are a confound for fine-detail comparison.

cost.note: Includes preparation, failed compatibility attempts and successful run; delayed accounting prevents treating per-attempt snapshot deltas as an isolated invoice.
